headline: Legal AI company Legora launched Skills, ready-made and customer-made instructions that tell its AI agent how to do specific legal tasks.
score_reason: Real product update, but announced Monday 5 Oct, before the window; score lowered by 1.
importance_line: Law firms and legal teams can save their own way of doing tasks such as contract review for the agent to repeat, though how well the skills work has not been reported.
summary: Law.com reports that Legora, a legal AI company, announced Legora Skills on Monday 5 Oct 2026: written instructions that tell its AI agent how to perform specific tasks. The launch library has more than 250 skills built by Legora's legal engineers, such as first-pass contract review and nondisclosure agreement triage, and customers can create their own through the agent's chat based on earlier work.
notes: Announced Monday 5 Oct 2026 per Law.com: score lowered by 1 (6 to 5). Article text was short (teaser only).
